free_tier.stated: Dynamic Port Forwarding, an exclusive feature for Premium members. The free tier carries 10 GB per month: For our Free users, you can use one device and 10 GB per month.

egress.terms: With the hide.me VPN Premium plan you can use unlimited data traffic and up to 10 devices simultaneously.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: In-app activation, or the @pf suffix on the username for manual clients.
tooling: Official app with the port-forwarding menu, or any client with the @pf username suffix.
chaining: Works as a throwaway endpoint for a test on a free VM; a DNS record pointing at it will rot.

limits.value: static port forwarding is refused outright: hide.me views static port forwarding as a potential security concern. Due to this, we refrain from permitting static port forwarding across our VPN server network. Instead, we introduce Dynamic Port Forwarding.

the mapping is UPnP-negotiated by the application rather than reserved by the account, so it is not addressable across a reconnect: Once the application maps a port, it can be contacted from the public Internet as though it is running on the router

binding_note: There is no byte quota on Premium, so volume does not bind. The refusal of static forwarding does: the vendor will not give a port that persists, which removes the stable public address the ingress test asks for.

identity_cost.detail: Premium purchase with card, PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, SEPA, SOFORT, bank transfer or crypto; the free tier needs no payment.

reliability_note: UPnP negotiation is per session; if a user's UPnP request is not repeated the mapping disappears with no server-side notice.
confidence_note: Measured would need a Premium account and a UPnP negotiation observed. Prices were taken from the vendor page as indexed rather than rendered, because the page body served was FAQ text only; the forwarding sentences were read directly.

evidence.proved: Dynamic port forwarding only, Premium only, no static forwarding on the network, and the @pf username suffix for manual connections.

The forwarding is UPnP, in-house server implementation, Premium only, and the mapping is requested by the application rather than reserved by the account; the failure case is described as No incoming TCP connections will get established, nor will UDP responses be sent in the proper manner, which is why ingress is recorded as tcp+udp.
Free users get one device and 10 GB per month; Premium gets unlimited data traffic and up to 10 devices.

Indexed price rows: 1 month $11.99, 24 months plus 4 extra at $2.50 per month billed $69.99 every 28 months, 12 months plus 2 extra at $3.93 per month billed $54.99. The rendered page served FAQ text only.

price_per_tb_month: USD 11.99 per month; USD 2.50 per month on 28 months (69.99); USD 3.93 per month on 14 months (54.99)
notes: The forum thread that surfaced first told users to buy a static IP, which supports the third reading, and the help page's own wording supports the second. Both can hold at once, and neither yields a free stable port.

extras.wg_detail: Manual connections are supported with a username suffix rather than an app: make sure you add the @pf suffix to your username if you intend to use the port forwarding feature. A user still configures the tunnel itself, which is what a WireGuard config does.
extras.volume_stated: With the hide.me VPN Premium plan you can use unlimited data traffic and up to 10 devices simultaneously.
extras.transit_note: Traffic crosses hide.me servers on the selected location.
